=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1513 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The root hook omits the approved read-loop exemption present in its workflow-template twin, causing approved literal-ID read loops to prompt and the parity/read-loop tests to fail.
  WHY: The reported seven test failures make the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job and aggregate CI check fail, blocking merge.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:339 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The environment-assignment checks do not recognize Bash append assignments such as `NAME+=value`, so a guarded Git command following one can be skipped.
  WHY: The highest reported severity is BLOCKER; reviewers disagree, with reports ranging from MAJOR to BLOCKER.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:466-475 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A `git push origin HEAD` refspec is treated as a push to a literal branch named `HEAD`, rather than resolving to the actual destination branch.
  WHY: The guard can query for PRs on `HEAD`, find none, and allow a push from a branch whose PR has merged.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:471-475 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The source-ref whitelist rejects valid Git revision expressions such as `HEAD~1` and `HEAD^`, causing the guard to discard the explicit destination and fall back to the session checkout.
  WHY: That fallback checks a different branch or worktree context and can produce a false block or miss a block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:432-475 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: When the remote is supplied with `--repo`, the parser still assumes the first positional argument is the remote and can discard the only refspec.
  WHY: The guard may inspect the current branch instead of the explicit destination branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:318-323 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The directory parser clears the resolved working directory at an `||` operator, losing the worktree context for a subsequent Git command.
  WHY: The guard may inspect the session checkout instead of the directory where the shell runs the push.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:255-271, 417-475 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Shell redirection file descriptors can be tokenized as positional arguments and treated as refspecs.
  WHY: The guard can inspect a bogus refspec or fall back to the session checkout rather than correctly evaluating the push target.
- scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh:248-256 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The Claude-engine transfer call does not redirect stderr to the attempt-scoped transfer-reason file.
  WHY: On transfer failure, the failure evidence reports `unknown` instead of the helper's diagnostic reason code; severity reports range from NIT to MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:432-445, 438 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Abbreviated inline push options such as `--push-op=ci.skip` are not recognized and may be treated as positional refspecs.
  WHY: The parser may fall back to checking the session checkout instead of the intended destination.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:471 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The destination-ref handling does not preserve a destination such as `HEAD~1`, so the guard falls back to checking the session checkout.
  WHY: The explicit destination ref is lost and the intended destination is not evaluated.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:437-444, 451, 1292 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A bulk push target is evaluated using only the worktree's current branch rather than all branches the push can affect.
  WHY: A push such as `git push origin --all` can include merged-only PR branches that the guard does not inspect.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "For `git push <remote> HEAD:<ref>` or `<src>:<ref>`, check the **target ref** (`<ref>`) for a merged PR with no open PR, not the local branch name. A detached HEAD pushing to an open PR's branch must be allowed."
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py around _push_targets, specifically the line handling refspecs without a colon (lines 466-475) and the destination-branch validator (lines 471-475)
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The cited code treats `git push origin HEAD` as branch `HEAD`; it has no special case resolving `HEAD` in an uncolonised refspec to the current branch.
- requirement: "Keep the §21.D budget: one cached REST call per (slug, branch) pair judged."
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py, the pr_snapshots dictionary and its writes
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The cache is keyed on `(slug, branch)` while ancestry checks also depend on each `_GuardTarget` source tip, so refspecs for the same branch with different tips can reuse a PR list with the wrong tip.
- requirement: "Acceptance: tests in `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` cover all of these: ... `git -C <path>` behaves the same way"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py — the `test_git_dash_c_allows_detached_worktree_open_destination` test asserts returncode 0 for `git -C WT push origin HEAD:feature/open`, but does NOT test the merged-destination case via `git -C`
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The cited test covers the open-destination case; the evidence also says the merged-destination case is covered by `test_worktree_push_to_merged_branch_from_other_checkout` and identifies the open-destination case for `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` as uncovered.
- requirement: "Cover these cases in guard tests and keep the workflow-template hook byte-identical."
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The cited review reports seven test failures because `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` lacks the read-loop clause present in its workflow-template twin; the requirement also calls for guard-test coverage.
- requirement: "Keep the `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/` twin byte-identical."
  expected_change_site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The cited review says the `pr_merge_status_guard.py` twins are byte-identical but `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1513` lacks the condition present in `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py:1514`.
- requirement: "Resolve the effective repository for each guarded git command: the last `cd <path>` before it in the same command line, `git -C <path>`, or `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` prefixes."
  expected_change_site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_guarded_git_invocations` and `_push_targets`
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The review identifies append assignments at line 339, `cd ... || exit 1` at line 322, `--repo <remote>` at line 451, and `git push origin HEAD` at lines 466-467 as cases where the effective repository or target is not handled as required.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
